listed_sector_signals.signal: Stray reference to energy management 'in the paper manufacturing process' tied to ISO 50001 (appears to be a copy-paste artifact but names pulp & paper explicitly)
listed_sector_signals.quote:
Energy management in the paper manufacturing process is based on the Cuban standard ISO 50001: 2019 and a methodology 
for energy use [9].

other_continuous_flow_signals.signal: Sugar cane mill with continuous crushing/steam generation as the actual study object
other_continuous_flow_signals.quote:
The sugar mill has a crushing capacity of 2,700 t/d. The 
steam supply consists of a water tube boiler with a superheated 
steam generation capacity of 60 t/h at 1.34 MPa and 318   oC, which 
consumes bagasse.

other_continuous_flow_signals.signal: Cogeneration unit of the sugar mill for surplus electricity production
other_continuous_flow_signals.quote:
Retrofitting a sugar mill's cogeneration unit for the purpose 
of surplus electricity production may not always be feasible due to, 
among other things, the seasonality of sugar cane production

other_continuous_flow_signals.signal: Adjacent alcohol/ethanol distillery consuming molasses, juices and steam
other_continuous_flow_signals.quote:
An 
alcohol distillery near the sugar mill consumes the molasses, juices 
and steam from the first-effect evaporator.

one_line: The paper applies energy analysis and pinch/heat-integration methods (Aspen Energy Analyzer) to a real sugar cane mill to identify energy and water savings and design a heat exchanger network; sugar milling is not a listed Corpus B sector, and the only listed-sector mention (pulp & paper) is a stray phrase.
